name: Pavement
label: Matador
lede: Two guys from Stockton cut a record in a hippie drummer's house, got pelted with mud at Lollapalooza, quit with handcuffs on the mic stand, and came back to find a B-side had become their biggest song.

eras.title: Two aliases and a hippie's studio
eras.text: Pavement started as a studio project, not a band: Stephen Malkmus and Scott Kannberg, calling themselves S.M. and Spiral Stairs, recording in a Stockton, California house studio owned by a drummer twenty years older than them. The early singles sounded like static with a songwriter hiding inside.

years.h: Malkmus and Kannberg start Pavement in Stockton
years.p: [[Stephen Malkmus|eaefd603-84c1-4db4-a72b-0cb718a0cc07]] and [[Scott Kannberg|632a2bce-6f80-458b-a375-649ddffb03e0]] form Pavement as a recording project under the names S.M. and Spiral Stairs.

q: This Malkmus idiot is a complete songwriting genius.
years.h: Slay Tracks: 1933–1969, cut at Gary Young's house
years.p: The debut EP is recorded at [[Gary Young|95aa5cf9-b2c0-4d3c-a6e9-841d79cb24a1]]'s home studio, Louder Than You Think. Young, a local hippie drummer, ends up playing on it and joining.
years.xp:
Young was blunt about the kid he was recording. He said, per Wikipedia, that Malkmus was a songwriting genius, in less polite words.

A drummer named Jason Turner briefly replaced Young in 1989 and left over clashes with Malkmus, who later called him competitive and depressed.

years.h: Pavement's first performance is on KDVS college radio
years.p: Pavement's first ever performance goes out live on KDVS-FM, the college station in Davis, California.

years.h: Demolition Plot J-7 EP on Drag City
years.p: Chicago's Drag City puts out the second Pavement EP. A guitarist, Rob Chamberlin, passes through the line-up the same year.

years.h: Bob Nastanovich and Mark Ibold join Pavement
years.p: Malkmus's New York roommate [[Bob Nastanovich|4bcaf5b5-89a5-4712-8a11-6d60dd0904f5]] joins on percussion and shouting, and [[Mark Ibold|003db9eb-2a01-4ece-a5e0-87000aa502d7]] takes bass. The live band exists at last.

years.h: Perfect Sound Forever EP
years.p: The third Pavement EP, recorded at Gary Young's studio like the first two.

eras.title: Handstands, cabbages and a hotel in Copenhagen
eras.text: Slanted and Enchanted passed around on dubbed cassettes before it came out and changed what indie rock sounded like. Onstage, Gary Young was the show, until his drinking made the show impossible.

years.h: Slanted and Enchanted · Matador
years.p: Pavement's debut album spreads on tape before its release on Matador Records. It later lands on Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Albums of All Time.
years.xp: Recorded at Gary Young's Louder Than You Think, it became one of the most cited indie rock albums of the 1990s: fractured songs, heavy distortion and stream-of-consciousness words over a lo-fi hiss.

years.h: Gary Young hands out cabbage and mashed potatoes to fans
years.p: On the Slanted and Enchanted tour, drummer [[Gary Young|95aa5cf9-b2c0-4d3c-a6e9-841d79cb24a1]] greets crowds with vegetables, does handstands and falls off his stool drunk.
years.xp: Malkmus later said the band knew Young was a flaky hippie, but hadn't known how bad his drinking problem was.

years.h: Gary Young quits after a meeting in a Copenhagen hotel
years.p: After a 1993 tour of Australia, Japan and Europe, Bob Nastanovich, Young's best friend in the band, argues with him at a Copenhagen hotel. [[Gary Young|95aa5cf9-b2c0-4d3c-a6e9-841d79cb24a1]] agrees to leave.

years.h: Steve West debuts at a Drag City festival in Chicago
years.p: [[Steve West|c4705a05-ffdd-4441-a852-0aeb94de4c9b]] takes over the drums and plays his first Pavement show at a Drag City festival in Chicago.

years.h: Pavement's R.E.M. tribute on No Alternative
years.p: Pavement's song Unseen Power of the Picket Fence, a love letter to [[R.E.M.|ea4dfa26-f633-4da6-a52a-f49ea4897b58]], appears on the Red Hot Organization's AIDS-benefit compilation No Alternative.

eras.title: The band that ruined Lollapalooza
eras.text: Crooked Rain, Crooked Rain put Pavement on MTV and late-night TV, and one song on it started a feud with a headliner. A year later the band made its most sprawling record and got mud thrown at it.

years.h: Crooked Rain, Crooked Rain and the MTV hit Cut Your Hair
years.p: The second album gives Pavement its only real brush with the mainstream: Cut Your Hair on MTV and alternative radio, and a spot on The Tonight Show with Jay Leno.

years.h: Range Life starts a feud with Billy Corgan
years.p: Pavement's Range Life takes shots at [[The Smashing Pumpkins|ba0d6274-db14-4ef5-b28d-657ebde1a396]] and [[Stone Temple Pilots|8c32bb01-58a3-453b-8050-8c0620edb0e5]]. [[Billy Corgan|3cbfd3e3-6d9b-4327-84ba-42cf646c98f9]] threatens to pull the Pumpkins from headlining Lollapalooza 1994 if Pavement plays.
years.xp:
Malkmus said the song was light-hearted and sung from the view of an aging hippie character. Corgan did not take it that way.

The Pumpkins headlined; Pavement did not play the 1994 tour. They got their turn the next summer.

years.h: Wowee Zowee, 18 tracks of everything
years.p: Punk, country and ballads on one long, restless record. Malkmus later said he was smoking a lot of grass and his picks for singles sounded like hits to him.

years.h: Lollapalooza crowds pelt Pavement with mud and rocks
years.p: On the 1995 Lollapalooza tour Pavement skips setlists for loose, drug- and drink-fueled jams. Crowds throw mud and rocks, and the band leaves the stage.
years.xp: Afterwards they called themselves The Band That Ruined Lollapalooza.

eras.title: Scrabble, Godrich and handcuffs
eras.text: Pavement got tidier and more tired at the same time. Terror Twilight brought in Radiohead's producer, the sessions stalled over board games, and the band ended at Brixton without anyone saying the word.

years.h: Brighten the Corners, produced by Mitch Easter
years.p: Shorter, straighter songs, with Stereo and Shady Lane as singles. [[Mitch Easter|b11c5ba2-495b-4d55-ab9b-52682cf2b81b]], of R.E.M.'s early records, produces.

years.h: Terror Twilight: Nigel Godrich and a lot of Scrabble
years.p: Sessions at Jackpot! in Portland stall while the band plays Scrabble. [[Nigel Godrich|52de022d-5401-427f-8301-ff1b8be11a7a]] takes over, moving to Sonic Youth's Manhattan studio and then RPM near Washington Square Park.
years.xp:
Godrich was hired to make a record that stood up straighter. He wanted more takes than Pavement was used to giving.

Nastanovich said Godrich only connected with Malkmus and still didn't know the others' names after several days.

years.h: After Coachella, Malkmus tells Pavement he wants out
years.p: After Pavement's set at the 1999 Coachella Festival, [[Stephen Malkmus|eaefd603-84c1-4db4-a72b-0cb718a0cc07]] tells his bandmates he doesn't want to go on.

q: These symbolize what it's like being in a band all these years.
years.h: Last show at Brixton: handcuffs on Malkmus's mic stand
years.p: Pavement's final concert is at Brixton Academy in London. [[Stephen Malkmus|eaefd603-84c1-4db4-a72b-0cb718a0cc07]] hangs handcuffs from his mic stand and tells the crowd what they stand for.
years.xp: Nobody announced a breakup that night. Nastanovich later said there was too much exhaustion for heavy emotion.

years.h: Steve West learns Pavement is over from the internet
years.p: Malkmus phones Kannberg to say they are no longer a band and tells him to update the website. The others find out online; West says nobody in the band ever called him.

eras.title: Central Park and a smashed guitar
eras.text: With Malkmus and Kannberg off in Stephen Malkmus and the Jicks and Preston School of Industry, Pavement became a DVD, a biography and a question. In 2010 they answered it with a world tour, a hometown show and one ugly night in Las Vegas.

years.h: Lance Bangs's Slow Century documentary
years.p: Lance Bangs releases Slow Century, a two-DVD set of every Pavement video and concert footage back to 1989.

years.h: Pavement's reunion confirmed, Central Park sells out fast
years.p: Brooklyn Vegan breaks the news of Central Park shows, the band confirms on September 17 and 18, and Central Park tickets sell out in two minutes. Three more shows are added.

years.h: The Pavement reunion tour opens in Auckland
years.p: Pavement's first show in over ten years is in Auckland, New Zealand, the start of a year-long world tour.

years.h: First Stockton show ever, with Gary Young back on drums
years.p: Pavement finally plays its hometown, at the Bob Hope Theatre. [[Gary Young|95aa5cf9-b2c0-4d3c-a6e9-841d79cb24a1]] comes out for the encore and plays three songs from Slanted and Enchanted.

years.h: Kannberg smashes his guitar at Matador at 21 in Las Vegas
years.p: At Matador's 21st-birthday weekend at the Palms Casino, [[Scott Kannberg|632a2bce-6f80-458b-a375-649ddffb03e0]] kicks his monitor and smashes his guitar. NME notes an icy atmosphere onstage.

eras.title: A B-side goes viral
eras.text: Pavement came back as a band whose old fans had kids, and whose new fans had found them on TikTok. The second reunion outlasted the first, lost Gary Young, and got a musical, a movie and finally a new song.

years.h: Pavement announces a Primavera Sound reunion
years.p: Pavement books two Primavera Sound sets for 2020. The pandemic pushes them to 2022.

years.h: Harness Your Hopes goes viral, twenty years late
years.p: Harness Your Hopes, a 1999 B-side from the Spit on a Stranger EP, spreads on TikTok and becomes Pavement's most-streamed song.

years.h: First show since 2010, at the Fonda in Los Angeles
years.p: Pavement's second reunion starts with a sold-out Fonda Theatre show. [[Rebecca Cole|9a8de0df-12bf-41ed-8752-46cfcec70923]] of [[The Minders|a0cf076f-2fa8-476a-84e2-6d9980c0deb9]] and [[Wild Flag|4473e47b-81bb-47af-8cb0-1cad6f68d8bc]] joins on keyboards, and tours of North America and Europe follow.

years.h: Slanted! Enchanted! opens off-Broadway
years.p: Slanted! Enchanted! A Pavement Musical opens in New York, built from Pavement songs around a Malkmus-like hero.

years.h: Louder Than You Think, the Gary Young film, at SXSW
years.p: A documentary about Pavement's first drummer premieres at SXSW.

years.h: Gary Young dies at 70
years.p: [[Gary Young|95aa5cf9-b2c0-4d3c-a6e9-841d79cb24a1]], Pavement's original drummer and the owner of the studio where it all started, dies at 70.

years.h: Pavement plays The National's Homecoming in Cincinnati
years.p: Billed as the last show for a while, at Smale Park during [[The National|664c3e0e-42d8-48c1-b209-1efca19c0325]]'s Homecoming festival.

years.h: Pavements premieres at the New York Film Festival
years.p: Pavement plays a one-off at Sony Hall in New York for the premiere of Pavements, the film about the band. Nastanovich calls it the last show for a long time.

years.h: First new Pavement song in 25 years
years.p: Scott Kannberg says the Pavements soundtrack will carry a new Pavement song, the first in over twenty-five years.

years.h: A short 2026 tour, from Mosswood Meltdown to Shaky Knees
years.p: Pavement plays a brief run that opens at Mosswood Meltdown in Oakland and ends September 19 at Shaky Knees in Atlanta.
